title: Excerpts from "A Philosophy of Software Design"
summary: John Ousterhout's core design principles: minimizing complexity through deep modules with simple interfaces, information hiding, strategic programming over tactical shortcuts, and designing it twice before implementation; managing complexity through error definition, documentation as design tool, and avoiding intuition-driven optimization.
when-to-read: When you're facing questions about how to structure modules, reduce system complexity, or decide between competing design approaches for a major component. If you're looking for guidance on code organization at a high level, see software-architecture; if you need testing strategy specifically, consult the testing tag.
